cases.name: union-discriminated-oneof
cases.note: a discriminated union in oneOf mode: three tagged members, tags distinct

cases.name: union-discriminated-anyof
cases.note: the same discriminated members in anyOf mode — the mode is identity in the carrier and is not consulted by the denotation

cases.name: union-discriminated-singleton
cases.note: a one-member discriminated union — the bare (unwrapped) arm of ElMembers

cases.name: struct-with-union
cases.note: a discriminated union under a struct field — the denotation composes

cases.name: union-undiscriminated-anyof
cases.note: an undiscriminated anyOf union over keywords — admitted as content, El is Empty, so no value triples exist (corpus restriction 3)

cases.name: union-undiscriminated-oneof
cases.note: an undiscriminated oneOf union over two string literals, spelled zebra before alpha — order is identity

cases.name: union-nested
cases.note: a union whose second member is a union — the no-flattening rule, admitted

cases.name: tuple-pair
cases.note: a two-element tuple — admitted as content, El is Empty (corpus restriction 7), and position is identity

cases.name: tuple-pair-swapped
cases.note: the same two element types in the other order — a DIFFERENT code at a different address

cases.name: tuple-optional-element
cases.note: a trailing optional element — the optionality bit is carried, never collapsed; whether an optional element may sit anywhere but last is a DENOTATION question, not an admission one

cases.name: tuple-with-rest
cases.note: Schema.TupleWithRest: one element and a rest type — the rest is an Option in the carrier, so at most one is structural

cases.name: tuple-nested
cases.note: a tuple inside an array inside a tuple — nesting like any other code

cases.name: array-plain-still-array
cases.note: the plain array, unchanged by the Arrays completion: {elements:[], rest:[t]} has NO tuple spelling, because Ast.tuple takes a first element — which is what keeps the revision-1 projection injective with no second collapse

cases.name: enum-string
cases.note: a string enum spelled Up before Down — admitted as content, El is Empty (corpus restriction 6), and the order is Object.keys order, which is source order

cases.name: enum-string-reversed
cases.note: the same two members in the other order — a DIFFERENT code at a different address: order is identity for enums as it is for unions

cases.name: enum-number-alias
cases.note: a numeric enum with a negative member and an ALIAS (two names at one value) — admitted, because the NAME is the member's identity and TypeScript spells aliases

cases.name: struct-with-enum
cases.note: an enum under a struct field: the struct's own El is uninhabited too, so it carries no value triples

cases.name: decl-date
cases.note: effect/schema/Date, arity 0, null payload — admitted as content; El is Empty, so no value triples exist (corpus restriction 4)

cases.name: decl-url
cases.note: effect/schema/URL, arity 0, null payload

cases.name: decl-option-str
cases.note: effect/schema/Option at arity 1 over String — the one arity-1 row

cases.name: decl-option-nested
cases.note: Option over a struct — the type parameter is a code like any other

cases.name: struct-with-decl
cases.note: a declaration under a struct field: the struct's own El is uninhabited too, so it carries no value triples

cases.name: annotation
cases.note: the sidecar annotation kind: key, a subject union over the thirteen addressable planes — the meta and agent five (0x53 schema, 0x54 system, 0x58 exchange, 0x0F program, 0x47 git), the content four decision 40's rider CA-1 admitted (0x01 value, 0x08 chunk, 0x0B file, 0x0D context), and that decision's own four sorts (0x41 annotation, 0x49 agent, 0x51 query, 0x52 result) — and a value that is either text or a typed reference

cases.name: exchange
cases.note: the exchange kind: prompt, answer, and a subject union whose arms address the schema plane (0x53) and the exchange plane (0x58)

cases.name: refuse-struct-unsorted
cases.note: struct fields out of strict name order — the sortedness clause of Ast.wf

cases.name: refuse-struct-duplicate
cases.note: a struct declaring the same field name twice — strict order subsumes no-duplicates

cases.name: refuse-struct-unsorted-nested
cases.note: the sortedness clause failing inside a nested struct

cases.name: refuse-union-empty
cases.note: the empty union — that is Never, and Never is not admitted

cases.name: refuse-union-empty-nested
cases.note: the empty union under a struct field

cases.name: refuse-union-empty-member
cases.note: an empty union as a member of a well-formed union

cases.name: refuse-enum-empty
cases.note: the empty enum — like the empty union it admits nothing, which is Never, and Never is not admitted

cases.name: refuse-enum-duplicate-name
cases.note: an enum declaring the same member name twice — the name IS the member's identity, so it cannot repeat (values may, and do: see enum-number-alias)

cases.name: refuse-enum-empty-nested
cases.note: the empty enum under a struct field

cases.name: refuse-decl-payload
cases.note: effect/schema/Date carrying a string payload — the row admits null only

cases.name: refuse-decl-arity-short
cases.note: effect/schema/Option with no type parameter — arity 1 is the row's discipline

cases.name: refuse-decl-arity-long
cases.note: effect/schema/Date with a type parameter — arity 0 is the row's discipline

cases.name: refuse-decl-param-illformed
cases.note: an admitted declaration whose type parameter is an ill-formed code

cases.name: refuse-unknown-declaration
cases.note: effect/schema/Duration: a declaration shipping Effect's whole contract and no registry row — the allowlist is the admission rule (PLAN P4)

cases.name: refuse-unknown-declaration-nested
cases.note: the same unadmitted id under a struct property

cases.name: admit-references-table
cases.note: a revision-1 document allocating a reference table of non-recursive named entries — the shape Effect emits whenever one named schema is used twice

cases.name: admit-guarded-recursion
cases.note: the linked list exactly as Effect emits it: the root references the table and the recursive knot sits under a Suspend, so the cycle passes through a guard and resolution terminates

cases.name: refuse-unguarded-alias-cycle
cases.note: A is B and B is A, with no Suspend anywhere: resolving it never reaches a node. Effect's own codec reads this back without complaint, so the refusal is this door's alone

cases.name: refuse-unguarded-struct-cycle
cases.note: A = {next: A} spelled with a bare reference where Effect would have written a Suspend — a shape Effect never emits and the representation can still spell

cases.name: admit-reference-chain
cases.note: one acyclic edge: A names B and B is a code. The first admitted row whose bare-edge relation is not empty — a door that never follows an edge refuses it, and the whole corpus used to let one pass

cases.name: admit-reference-chain-two
cases.note: two edges, so the guardedness search recurses more than once before it settles the root

cases.name: refuse-unguarded-and-illformed
cases.note: a table entry that is BOTH on a bare cycle and out of field order — two defects, one name. The door names the cycle, and the TypeScript gate mirrors that order rather than naming whichever defect its own walk reached first

cases.name: refuse-duplicate-reference-key
cases.note: a references table naming A twice, the reference FIRST: Lean's parser keeps both pairs and takes the first, so the table cycles, and JSON.parse keeps the last, so it does not. Refused for the spelling before either reader decides anything

cases.name: refuse-duplicate-reference-key-last
cases.note: the same duplicate with the pairs swapped, which reverses which reader sees the cycle — the other direction of the split, and the same refusal

cases.name: admit-guarded-chain
cases.note: a GUARDED cycle whose bare relation is not empty: A names B bare and B reaches A again under a Suspend, so the search must follow a real edge AND stop at the guard. A door that does only one of the two passes every earlier admitted row and fails here

cases.name: refuse-partly-guarded-cycle
cases.note: one pair of names joined BOTH ways — A reaches B bare and again under a guard, B reaches A. The guarded path does not excuse the bare one: some-path-is-guarded is not the predicate, and a door that reads it that way admits a table whose resolution never finishes

cases.name: refuse-dead-unguarded-entry
cases.note: an unguarded cycle among entries the ROOT NEVER REACHES. Guardedness is a property of the table, not of the part of it the representation uses, so a door that walks from the root inward admits this. It is also where a dead entry stops being harmless: a dead well-formed entry is admitted, a dead cyclic one is not

cases.name: refuse-wrong-revision
cases.note: a schema-node envelope at a revision no door speaks

cases.name: refuse-unadmitted-node
cases.note: Effect's BigInt node — a first-order representation node the admitted subset defers

cases.name: refuse-union-mode
cases.note: a union at a mode outside the table — not a union spelling at all

cases.name: refuse-number-unchecked
cases.note: a bare Number with no isInt check — Effect's float-capable number, which the value plane has no term for (ruling 15, the float ceiling)

cases.name: refuse-number-check-alien
cases.note: a Number carrying effect/schema/isBetween — a check id the admitted subset does not reach (the checks layer is Slice C5)

cases.name: refuse-number-check-drift
cases.note: a Number whose isInt check is spelled with different annotations — the admitted subset pins ONE spelling of the one admitted check, so drift is not a schema

cases.name: refuse-string-checked
cases.note: a String carrying a filter — every admitted node but Number has an EMPTY checks list
cases.payload: {"revision":1,"value":{"references":{},"representation":{"_tag":"String","checks":[{"_tag":"Filter","aborted":false,"annotations":{"expected":"a value with a length of at least 2"},"representation":{"id":"effect/schema/isMinLength","payload":{"minLength":2}}}]}}}

cases.name: refuse-tuple-empty
cases.note: the EMPTY tuple, {elements:[], rest:[]} — Schema.Tuple([]) has no spelling in the carrier and had none before the Arrays completion either, so nothing is retired by refusing it

cases.name: refuse-tuple-rest-two
cases.note: an Arrays node with TWO rest types — the trailing-rest semantics the admission map defers; the carrier holds an Option, so the refusal is structural rather than a clause that could drift

cases.name: refuse-tuple-element-annotated
cases.note: an element carrying an annotation bag — annotations are GROW(C-ann), on elements as everywhere else

cases.name: refuse-enum-boolean-member
cases.note: an Enum whose member value is a boolean — Effect's Enum persists string and number values only, so this is not an enum spelling at all

cases.name: refuse-index-signature
cases.note: an Objects node with an index signature — records are Slice C3, not admitted yet

cases.name: refuse-mutable-property
cases.note: a property signature declaring isMutable — the mutability bit is not collapsed and only the immutable reading is admitted

restrictions: non-recursive: Ast has no Suspend/Reference constructor; a non-empty references table is a refusal case, never an admitted one (survey B3, ruling 2)
non-float: Cas.Json.Value has no float, so no float triple is writable at all (ruling 15, the float ceiling)
no undiscriminated-union values: El of an undiscriminated union is Empty, so Lean has no verdict for such a value; those codes carry admission verdicts only
no declaration values: El of a general declaration is Empty (the named declEl obligation); Date/URL/Option carry admission verdicts only
values are canonically spelled: every candidate is canonValue-normalized before its verdict is computed, so object key order is never the thing under test

no enum values: El of an enum is Empty (the named enumEl obligation) — WF admits alias members, so the index a value carries would be a function of member order rather than of the value; enums carry admission verdicts only

no tuple values: El of a tuple is Empty (the named tupleEl obligation) — an absent optional element shortens a JSON array rather than leaving a hole, so a non-trailing optional has no positional encoding at all; tuples carry admission verdicts only
